newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - July 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - July 7.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Foreign Minister Prachuab Chaiyasarn said if Cambodia ws not ready to join ASEAN, the regional group could delay membership until later this year. He said although the regional grouping agreed to admit Laos, Burma and Cambodia at the same time, Cambodia could join later if it was not prepared. He said ASEAN foreign minister would have to review the Cambodian situation when they meet later this month in Kuala Lumpur. (THE NATION)

- The Democrat Party may give up its plan to censure two prominent cabinet members if they improve their performance, deputy leader Banyat Bantadtan says. He says the opposition has no wish to add to the financial woes by launching the no-confidence motion against the government. (BANGKOK POST)

- Crime Investigation Bureau deputy commissioner Seri Temiyavej has dismissed doubts about his right to suppress illegal bookmaking at two horse racecourses in Bangkok. The response comes after Metropolitan Police Bureau commissioner Police Lt Gen Sophon Varatchanond questions whether the CIB deputy commissioner has the authority to suppress the activities at the Royal Sports Club and the Royal Turf Club. (BANGKOK POST)

- After almost 10 years of protesting against the second-stage expressway -- which is designed to cut through their communities -- Baan Krua residents have not backed down from their original platform and have sworn to fight the project to the death. This extreme stand has been taken in response to an ultimatum by the Expressway and Rapid Transit Authority of Thailand that residents move before September. (THE NATION)

- The Council of Economic Ministers will today announce measures to control the prices of fuel and essential goods to cushion the impact from the flotation of the baht, Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh says. Authorities have been checking the prices of goods at various markets and find no substantial increase in the prices of basic commodities. (BANGKOK POST)

- Phatra Thanakit Plc has decided to adopt the purchase and assumption (P&A) method for all its mergers. In the report submitted to the Bank of Thailand, Phatra, as one of five core finance and securities companies to merge with financially-collapsed finance companies also promises to manage the bad assets left over from the mergers. (THE NATION)
